workLog.action: Audited the live model-pin state against ADR-080 rule 1 for issue #2840
workLog.result: git grep found three skills still carrying a versioned Claude id (programming-advisor claude-opus-4-6, security-scan and style-enforcement claude-sonnet-4-6), contradicting the 2026-07-22 status that skills were fully de-versioned.

workLog.action: Traced why scripts/validation/check_model_pins.py reported zero violations on those three files
workLog.result: parse_frontmatter is line-based: its key regex is anchored at column 0, so an indented key under a nested mapping is dropped and metadata collapses to an empty string. The parser already yaml.safe_loads the block for validation and then discards the typed structure.

workLog.action: Exposed the already-computed typed structure instead of adding a second parser
workLog.result: Added FrontmatterResult.typed in scripts/validation/skill_frontmatter.py; additive dataclass field with a default factory, so every existing caller is unaffected (643 validation tests still pass).

workLog.action: Taught check_model_pins.py to see a pin nested below the top level and to reject it outright
workLog.result: A nested pin fails regardless of alias, rationale, or manifest evidence, because no harness reads the key: it is pure drift. Running the gate surfaced exactly the three known files and nothing else.

workLog.action: Removed the three nested versioned pins and regenerated the customer-facing mirrors
workLog.result: build_all.py propagated the deletion to src/copilot-cli/skills; git grep for a nested claude- id across both trees returns nothing. Both plugin manifests bumped to 0.6.103 and parity confirmed.

workLog.action: Ran two negative controls with teeth
workLog.result: Blinding the gate to nested pins fails 3 of the 6 new tests; dropping the parser's typed field fails 4. Restoring both returns 27 passed.

workLog.task: Close the three bypasses an adversarial review found in the nested-pin check
workLog.outcome: All three merited and all three were the same design error: the detector answered 'is there a nested pin' with a single value when the honest answer is a list. (1) A compliant top-level alias hid every nested pin, because _classify_and_read only walked below the top level when the top-level model was absent. That is a one-line laundering path: keep the versioned id under metadata and satisfy the gate with an alias above it. (2) The first nested hit masked every later one, so a two-pin file reported one and the second survived the commit that fixed the first. (3) A self-referential YAML anchor raised RecursionError, which reads as a broken gate rather than a broken file. _nested_pins now returns every occurrence sorted by dotted path, runs unconditionally, and carries the recursion path as a cycle guard. write_baseline no longer writes a nested-only unit as an empty-string pin that a later comparison would read as matching. test_top_level_pin_wins_over_nested asserted bypass 1 as intended behavior and was replaced. Four new cases the old tests could not distinguish: two pins both reported, a pin outside metadata, a pin inside a list, a cyclic anchor. Four negative controls each fail only their own case. Gate output on the real tree is byte-identical before and after, so this closes bypasses without reclassifying anything that exists.

patterns.pattern: When a governance gate reports clean against a violation you can see, suspect the parser before the policy
patterns.context: check_model_pins.py had a correct ADR-080 rule for versioned skill pins and still passed three files that carried one.
patterns.application: Dump what the parser actually returns for the offending file. Here it returned metadata as an empty string, which located the hole in one step.

avoidances.antipattern: Hand-rolling a second frontmatter parse to reach data the shared parser already computed
avoidances.consequence: Two parsers drift apart and the next nested-key bug has to be fixed twice.
avoidances.correction: Expose the typed structure the shared parser already builds for validation, and read it from the caller.
